verdict.tagline: Deep ocean exploration that rewards curiosity and self-reliance.
for_you_if: you enjoy self-directed open world survival
you like uncovering mysteries without a waypoint
you want a smooth experience on modest hardware
not_for_you_if: you need clear guidance for progression
you are frustrated by buggy vehicle mechanics

distortion_flags.sentence: Player sentiment improves steadily from the opening hours into the deep endgame.

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Players starting out find the initial progression slow and unguided, struggling to figure out where to go next.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game lacks direction or guidance for story progression, leaving players without clear instructions on where to go.

citations.review_text: The game has no direction unless you analyze 100 different voicelines mid game and has unneccesarry amounts of travelling at times you are playing back and forth sim 1/10 playthrough experience it is at least pretty

Unfortunately, the story is simply not interesting enough to keep me engaged, and the early game is so slow that it really becomes tedious to even play, let alone try to actually progress. A game can be slow and still be good if executed properly and if the mechanics are good enough to stand on their own or if the slow nature of the progression complements the story. Here, though, neither is true.

Before I continue, I want to note that the visuals have a distinct style, the sound design is superb, and the atmosphere is done really well, but these are bogged down by everything else I'm going to touch on below.

After waking up in your lifepod, you're basically given no directions on where to go as far as story progression. For a sandbox game, that is fine; for a story or even a hybrid game, it's not. Swimming around, grabbing fish, and collecting resources is fun for a bit, but then you ask yourself, "What next?" Sometimes you'll find a data log or receive a radio message, which will point you to a lifepod, debris, abandoned structure, or some other thing related to the story, which is cool, but then the trail goes cold again for the next couple of in-game days until you receive the next scripted radio message, and then the cycle repeats. I wouldn't even really mind this if the world was cool enough to explore, which would then justify the wait, but after the initial novelty of the starting area evaporates, it becomes boring and repetitive. Maybe some late-game locations are cooler and more interesting to explore, I wouldn't know, but the game lost me here, and I don't think I'll be coming back anytime soon.

The survival mechanics and crafting honestly feel more tacked-on than anything else, because they're so simple and basic that they really feel like an afterthought, which doesn't help the game's case. For crafting specifically, all you have to do is learn the recipe, collect the resources, and click, at which point the fabricator thingy does everything else. Ev…

Ok it says I've played for 6 hrs I don't think that's true, maybe 6 hrs played while online? Because I probably played six hours of it the night I got it. I love the ocean, I love animals, I love exploring. I would reccomend this to any body who likes fo3/skyrim, BOTW/TOTK. It's a completely different vibe and story but they share a lot of elements. Though my only complaint is I often just don't know what I am supposed to do. I am someone who doesn't like spoilers or to look up the answers. But that could easily just be a me problem and I wouldn't dock a star for that. I really love this game.

perfect game i love it so much although buggy sometimes its really fun and even better with mods

citations.review_text: Halfway through - amazingly fun with many surprises. Instructions are minimal; exploration and curiosity are fundamental to achieving progress. Highly recommend NOT playing on absolute hardest difficulty first time around (dying in game means restarting) since you can easily die any number of ways. Overall and excellent game.

When i first played it i didnt know what to do .pda helped but not enought,There was a time when i hit a plato in the progress line and didnt know waht to do so i just spend most of the time (2-3 rl days)wondering waht to do.Maybe the developers should put some clues. claims.claim: Reviewers mention that crafting and base building lack certain quality-of-life features, which can be addressed using game modifications.

citations.review_text: So 50 hours to beat the game of which about 30 were peaceful diving in early to mid game and chasing radio signals, 5 hours were the final game with all the pain it is to go from point A to point B and at least 10 hours were literally crawling the ocean to find the missing pieces for what I needed to build and they never spawned until I went to the end of the map and beyond. So yeah, the ocean is beautiful, the adventure is fun, until there is a story and then there is the total emptiness when the story ends. At least I made a nice base with a nuclear reactor next to my bedroom. But for new players: use mods - the bed-teleport mod is a life-saver also the resource scanner. Also know that you might write 1 cheat and then disable it and your achievements are gone. Yay.
Missing some QOL stuff in the crafting and base building department, but those can be fixed with mods if they bug you. Other than that, amazing game that is so immersive.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the progression as being driven by a tech tree and exploration, with story elements initially guiding the player before leaving them to figure out how to proceed on their own.

citations.review_text:
PepperTuna's Rate-O-Meter: 0 NO, 1 terrible, 2 bad, 3 subpar, 4 mediocre, 5 average, 6 decent, 7 good, 8 great, 9 amazing, 10 my favourite. Rating: 8 (great) or 9 (amazing).

Gameplay: The player manages 4 stats: Healthpoints, hunger, thirst and oxygen, with thirst draining faster than hunger and oxygen drain and quantity being dependent on your equipment and depth underwater. Progression is tech tree-driven with the bulk of playtime being well-paced as a result of this, as you need to explore to find resources and blueprints to craft equipment that lets you explore ever-further. Pacing starts to taper off in the late-game and can be a slog at the endgame. Certain story elements are used to kickstart progression and guide the player in the right direction by giving them waypoints, but after that they are (literally) left in the deep end on how to progress, which can cause friction if not patient or explorative enough. As this is an open world survival-craft game, you may have a vastly different experience from the next player. You might spend over 100 hours devoted largely to base building, or maybe you'll rush through in 15 hours without any change in pace. Base building works as follows: Place the start of your base anywhere, then make it branch out in what's essentially a grid. You can decorate the interiors, however there's only so much flexibility with what you're given.

Play Level: You are free to choose which direction you explore, limited only by your equipment and in the late-game the terrain too. You start out in the middle of the map, and going in any direction will eventually lead you closer to the ending. You will need to travel between various points on the map, though with how resources are spread some areas aren't vital to visit for progression or story completion. Terrain naturally guides your eye towards POIs, take for example a canyon leading towards a wreck you can loot, rather than over-relying on yellow paint methods of guiding the player. The…

My first survival game, and it certainly did not disappoint!

The concept of having most of the game take place underwater is refreshing, especially since getting your bearings in such an environment can be quite challenging. Exploration is at the heart of the experience, with different biomes to discover, each presenting its own challenges.

I did have to consult a few guides along the way, as there were times when I felt the story wasn't progressing. More often than not, the answer lay in an area I hadn't explored yet. This does mean the game requires a significant time commitment, particularly if you want to figure things out on your own.

The sense of progression is very satisfying. As you discover and craft new tools and equipment, exploring the more challenging biomes becomes easier. However, the game never lets you feel completely invincible, maintaining a sense of danger and vulnerability throughout.

What kept me going was the intriguing story, which gradually unfolds as you explore. It was ultimately my biggest motivation to see the game through to the end.

single_points.text: One reviewer says that the game had quite a few glitches that caused them to have to start the game over at least once, losing all progress because the save became unplayable.

citation.review_text: Absolutely loved this game. I'd seen many clips over the years and thought I might be interested in it, but never pushed play and actually dove in. Was finally convinced to give it a try; sooooooooo glad I finally took the plunge! What a great story, experience and a unique send-off for future players. Love, love, love. My only complaint is that the game had quite a few glitches that caused me to have to start the game over at least once losing all my progress because the glitch was so bad it made that game save unplayable. Would still play again though, even knowing I might run into that issue again.
